findings.evidence: _NUMBER = re.compile(r"(?<![\w.])(\d...") -> numbers('Rs.500')==set(), numbers('approx.900')==set(), numbers('No.5')==set(). verify('Prices in the city market rose sharply and onions now cost Rs.900 per kilogram this week [1].', ['Prices in the city market rose sharply and onions now cost Rs.500 per kilogram this week.']) -> claim KEPT, dropped=[]. Same for 'approx.900' vs 'approx.100'. EV.evaluate on two pages 'Rs.500' vs 'Rs.900' -> conflicts 0 (with 'Rs 500'/'Rs 900' -> conflicts 1). Surface still says 'citations checked against the sources (wording, numbers, negation)'.
findings.expected: W1-AC10: a sentence whose numbers do not occur in the cited source is dropped; W1-AC11: differing numbers are reported as a conflict.
findings.suggested_minimal_fix: Extract digit runs regardless of a preceding letter or dot (e.g. lookbehind (?<![\d,]) only, or a separate pass that pulls every \d+(?:[.,]\d+)* token), and add regression cases for 'Rs.500', 'approx.900', 'No.5'.
findings.title: Citation verifier and conflict detector ignore numbers preceded by a letter or dot (e.g. 'Rs.500'), so an unsupported number survives verify

findings.evidence: _words() splits only lower->Upper and [_-.:/], not acronym->Word or letter<->digit, and \b fails before a digit. field_is_sensitive({'type':'text','name':n,'value':'12345678'}) is False for OTPCode, SMSOTP, cvv2, CVV2, cvc2, ccv, mpin, MPIN, tpin, acctNumber, acct_no, cardExpiry, passcode2, pwd1. Real Chromium snapshot of <input name="OTPCode" value="482913"> and <input name="cvv2" value="123"> returns sensitive:false with the values; AssistCommands assist_ask with a FakeAdapter sends '482913' and '123' into the Brain request body.
findings.expected: A0-AC7: OTP, card (CVV) and password/PIN fields have their values removed before anything leaves the adapter.
findings.suggested_minimal_fix: In both layers split names also at acronym->Word ('OTPCode'->'otp code') and letter<->digit ('cvv2'->'cvv 2'); add cvv2/cvc2/ccv/mpin/tpin/acct; add these names to tricky_fields.html and the parity test.
findings.title: Redaction name matching still misses common OTP/CVV/PIN/password field names (F5 repair incomplete), in both Python and in-page JS

findings.evidence: asking => askId != null && answer == null (added in 1844b48); revoke() sets answer=null but leaves askId. Flutter probe test (3.47.7): grant -> ask -> assist.answer COMPLETE -> revoke -> grant: printed 'after re-grant: active=true asking=true answer=null'; the Ask button (enabled only when !a.asking) stays disabled, 'URI is reading what you shared…' is shown, and no poll or event ever clears it until the worker restarts.
findings.expected: After Stop and a new grant the user can ask again; no 'reading' indicator without a running ask.
findings.suggested_minimal_fix: In revoke() (and grant()) also set askId = null when no ask is running, or track asking with an explicit flag cleared in _finishAnswer/_resetForNewWorker; add a widget test for ask -> stop -> share -> ask.
findings.title: After an answered question, Stop then a new grant leaves Ask permanently disabled (introduced by the F4 UI repair)

findings.evidence: Probe with a fake clock in which each fetch takes 20 s, 3 feeds plus 5 URLs, deadline_s=90: elapsed_s=100.0, status TIMED_OUT. The provider and feed loops have no _expired check, so the overrun can be larger with slow providers.
findings.suggested_minimal_fix: Check _expired(t0) before each provider call and each feed fetch, and pass the remaining budget as the fetch deadline.
findings.title: Research time budget is not checked during the search and feed phases

findings.evidence: Expiry is applied lazily on the worker (_expire_if_due on the next require/snapshot), and the controller polls only while an ask or research is running. After the 30-minute TTL the scope chip keeps showing sharing/ACTIVE until the user's next command.

findings.suggested_minimal_fix: Refresh assist_status at expires_in_s (one timer), or emit an assist.state event on expiry.
findings.title: UI keeps showing an expired grant as ACTIVE
